requirements.statement: The platform shall allow XATA employees to create, manage, prioritize, track and complete personal and team TODO items.
XATA wants a simple centralized web application that provides a common place to manage TODOs, with the first release intentionally kept small and easy to use.
The platform shall provide a single system for managing TODO items.
The platform shall allow users to quickly create and update TODOs.
The platform shall provide visibility of open, completed and overdue work.
The platform shall allow team members to assign TODOs to one another.
The platform shall provide basic priority and due-date management for TODO items.
The platform shall provide a simple dashboard for work tracking.
System shall allow an authenticated user to create a TODO. (Priority: Must)
A TODO shall contain title, description, status, priority and due date. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to edit TODOs they own or are authorized to manage. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to mark TODOs as completed. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to assign a TODO to another authorized user. (Priority: Must)
System shall support Open, In Progress and Completed statuses. (Priority: Must)
System shall support Low, Medium, High and Critical priorities. (Priority: Must)
Users shall filter TODOs by status, priority, assignee and due date. (Priority: Must)
Users shall search TODOs by title or description. (Priority: Should)
In scope: user login and basic user profile.
In scope: view and delete TODOs (create and edit are covered by BR-001 and BR-003).
In scope: add description and optional notes to a TODO.
In scope: dashboard showing TODO status.
In scope: basic team view for assigned TODOs.
In scope: audit information such as created date and updated date for TODOs.
Employee role responsibilities: create/manage own TODOs; view assigned TODOs; update status.
Team Lead role responsibilities: create/assign TODOs; view team TODOs; monitor overdue work.
Administrator role responsibilities: manage users and basic platform configuration.
Dashboard shall show Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue counts. (Priority: Must)
Team Leads shall view TODOs assigned to their team members. (Priority: Must)
System shall maintain created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to delete TODOs where permitted. (Priority: Should)
System shall prevent unauthorized modification of another user's TODO. (Priority: Must)
System shall provide a web interface through supported browsers. (Priority: Must)
Create TODO: user enters title and description, selects priority and due date, optionally assigns to a user, and saves the TODO.
Manage TODO: user can view details, edit information, change status, change priority or due date, reassign where authorized, and delete where authorized.
Dashboard shall show a count of High/Critical priority TODOs.
A TODO must have a title.
A due date cannot be earlier than the creation date unless explicitly permitted.
Completed TODOs must have Completed status.
Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs, and users cannot modify TODOs outside their authorization.
Overdue means the due date has passed and the status is not Completed.
Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.
The initial release is web-based.
The first release uses a single enterprise environment.
A user can log in and create a TODO.
A TODO can be assigned, updated, and completed.
Dashboard counts correctly reflect TODO state.
Filtering and search return correct results.
The application meets the agreed NFRs.
XATA can complete the core TODO lifecycle without administrator assistance.
Normal page/API response time must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.
TODO create/update operation must complete in ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
Dashboard loading must complete in ≤ 3 seconds for 95% of requests.
Search/filter response must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
The platform must support at least 500 concurrent active users.
Monthly availability shall be ≥ 99.5%, excluding agreed maintenance windows.
Planned maintenance shall be communicated at least 24 hours in advance.
After an application failure, service shall be restored within 30 minutes.
The solution shall support growth in users and TODO volume without major redesign.
The solution shall support at least 100,000 TODO records initially.
Application services should be horizontally scalable where practical.
Database design shall support future growth beyond initial capacity.
All users shall be authenticated before protected functionality is accessed.
Authorization shall be role-based.
Users shall only access TODO data permitted by their role.
Data shall be encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS.
Sensitive credentials shall not be hard-coded.
If passwords are locally managed, they shall use secure industry-standard hashing.
The application shall protect against common web vulnerabilities, including injection, broken access control and XSS.
Administrative actions should be auditable.
TODO records shall have unique identifiers.
Required fields shall be validated server-side.
Updates shall not silently overwrite conflicting data.
Created and updated timestamps shall be stored consistently.
Referential integrity shall be maintained between TODOs and users.
Deleted data handling shall follow XATA's retention policy.
Core create/update/complete flow should require minimal steps.
UI shall be responsive for standard desktop and tablet screens.
Validation errors shall be understandable.
Status, priority and overdue items shall be visually distinguishable.
Common actions shall be discoverable without technical knowledge.
Target WCAG 2.1 AA principles where practical.
Keyboard navigation should support core workflows.
Form controls should have meaningful labels.
Text should have sufficient contrast and readable sizing.
Solution shall use modular, maintainable code.
Business logic shall be separated from presentation and persistence.
APIs and major components shall be documented.
Automated unit tests shall cover critical business logic.
Configuration shall be externalized from source code.
Logging shall support troubleshooting without exposing sensitive information.
Application errors shall be logged with sufficient troubleshooting context.
Health checks shall be available.
Key metrics should include request failures and response latency.
Logs should include correlation/request identifiers where appropriate.
Operational alerts should be configurable for service failures.
Production data shall be backed up according to an agreed schedule.
Backups shall be protected from unauthorized access.
Solution shall support restoration after major failure.
Target RPO is 15 minutes unless XATA agrees otherwise.
Target RTO is 30 minutes.
Solution shall support current versions of major enterprise browsers such as Chrome and Edge.
Browser-specific functionality shall be avoided unless approved.
APIs should use documented, versionable interfaces.
Solution shall collect only data required for TODO management.
Access to personal/team information shall follow XATA authorization rules.
Sensitive information shall not be written to application logs.
Data retention and deletion shall follow XATA policy.
Critical application/database components shall have documented recovery procedures.
Recovery procedures shall be tested periodically.
XBS shall document dependencies required to restore the service.
XBS shall demonstrate compliance with agreed NFRs through appropriate testing, evidence, configuration review and operational validation before production acceptance.
The Security NFR category has priority Must.
The Performance NFR category has priority Must.
The Availability NFR category has priority Must.
The Data Integrity NFR category has priority Must.
The Backup & Recovery NFR category has priority Must.
The Usability NFR category has priority Must.
The Maintainability NFR category has priority Must.
The Accessibility NFR category has priority Should.
The Advanced observability NFR category has priority Should.

open_questions.question: What response time or effort threshold does 'quickly create and update TODOs' imply? The term is not measurable as written.
How is 'overdue' defined, and which priority levels are included in 'basic priority' management?
Who may assign TODOs to whom, and how are 'team' and 'team members' defined (for example, membership, scope, or permissions)?
What content, metrics, and views must the 'simple dashboard for work tracking' include?
What defines 'simple' and 'intentionally small' for the first release, and which capabilities are explicitly out of scope?
The objective to 'reduce dependency on spreadsheets, email and chat' has no measurable target or baseline. Is it a success measure or a requirement, and if measurable, what is the target?
The supplied evidence contains no NFR content (for example performance, security, availability, accessibility, or supported platforms). Are NFR sources available that should be included?
What defines a user as 'authorized to manage' or an 'authorized user' for editing (BR-003) and assignment (BR-005)? No authorization rules or role mapping are specified.
What defines a 'team' for the Team Lead team view and the basic team view for assigned TODOs? Team membership and structure are not described.
How is 'overdue' determined and how is monitoring of overdue work expected to be performed (e.g., views, alerts)? No overdue criteria or monitoring mechanism is specified.
What is included in the 'basic user profile' and in 'basic platform configuration' administered by the Administrator? Neither scope is defined.
Is the list of audit information fields complete? The source says 'such as created date and updated date', which implies additional fields may be expected but none are named.
What content and behavior is expected for the dashboard showing TODO status? No metrics, filters, or audience are specified.
Is a due date mandatory when creating a TODO? BR-002 lists due date as a TODO attribute but does not state whether it is required or optional, and the format is not specified.

Which status changes may Employees make? The Employee role is said to 'update status', but BR-006 and BR-004 define only Open, In Progress, Completed and marking as completed; the permitted transitions are not defined.
Is the priority of BR-009 (search, 'Should') consistent with the in-scope list, which includes search without a priority? Confirm whether search is required for initial release.
What criteria define 'where permitted' for deleting TODOs (BR-013)? The roles, ownership rules, and conditions are not specified.
What criteria define 'where authorized' for reassigning and deleting TODOs (section 7.2)? Authorization rules are not specified.
Which browsers are 'supported' for the web interface (BR-015)? No browser list or versions are given.
What are the allowed priority values (for example, whether Critical and High are distinct from other levels), and how is 'Overdue' determined from the due date?
Who is authorized to permit a due date earlier than the creation date, and under what conditions is that exception granted?
What roles and permissions define 'authorized users' for assigning and modifying TODOs?
Which NFRs are the 'agreed NFRs' referenced in the acceptance criteria, and where are they documented? No NFR content is included in the supplied evidence.
Beyond 'Completed', which TODO status values exist, and what transitions between them are permitted?
NFR-PERF-001 refers to 'normal load' without defining it. What user volume, request rate, or operating conditions constitute normal load for the response-time target?

NFR-PERF-005 requires 'at least 500' concurrent active users but does not define 'active' or the measurement window. Must the 500 users be supported at peak, sustained, or at a specific response-time target, and what counts as an active user?

The NFR-PERF-001 to NFR-PERF-004 targets state '95% of requests' without specifying the measurement period or the load conditions under which the percentile is measured. Over what period and under what load should compliance be measured?
Which maintenance windows are 'agreed', who agrees them, and how are they documented? NFR-AVL-001 excludes them from the availability measure without defining them.
How is monthly availability measured (calendar month definition, measurement point, and how partial outages are counted)?
How is 'restored' defined for the 30-minute recovery target in NFR-AVL-003, and is the target measured from failure detection or from failure onset?
What growth targets (users, TODO volume, time horizon) apply beyond the initial 100,000 TODO records, and what counts as 'major redesign'?
Under what conditions is horizontal scalability considered 'practical', and is it required or only preferred?
Which user roles exist and which TODO data each role may access? The role model is not defined in the supplied evidence.
Which passwords are 'locally managed' versus externally managed, and what hashing standard is intended?
Which administrative actions must be auditable, and what audit records and retention are required? The 'should' obligation strength is not clarified.
What is XATA's retention policy referenced for deleted data, and where is it documented? The policy content is not supplied.
Which fields are 'required' for TODO records, and how should conflicting updates be detected and resolved?
What scope and success criteria apply to 'where practical' for targeting WCAG 2.1 AA principles, and which specific WCAG success criteria are required?

What is the measurable meaning of 'minimal steps' for the core create/update/complete flow, and what are the defined 'standard desktop and tablet screens' (sizes, resolutions, or devices)? Are mobile phone screens in scope?
Which business logic is considered 'critical' for the automated unit test coverage requirement, and is there a minimum coverage target?
In which cases are correlation/request identifiers considered 'appropriate' for logs, and what is the expected handling of sensitive information in logs?
What is the agreed backup schedule for production data, and who agrees it?
How will XATA agree to a different RPO than 15 minutes, and what process or approval applies?
Is the 15-minute RPO and 30-minute RTO a hard requirement or a target, and what scope (which data, components, or service) do they apply to?
What constitutes a 'major failure' for the restoration requirement, and what restoration time or success criteria apply?
Which browsers and versions make up 'major enterprise browsers' beyond Chrome and Edge, and who approves browser-specific functionality?
What is the required frequency for periodic recovery procedure testing?
What are the XATA authorization rules and XATA data retention and deletion policies referenced by the privacy requirements, and are they provided to the bidder?
What does 'XBS' refer to, and what is its role relative to the solution?

The priority table assigns Must or Should to NFR categories but does not state the underlying NFR statements, thresholds, units, or measurement criteria for each category. Which specific requirements sit under each category?
The source does not define the obligation strength of 'Must' versus 'Should'. Is a 'Should' category excluded from the production acceptance demonstration required by the NFR acceptance section?
The NFR acceptance section refers to 'agreed NFRs' but the supplied evidence does not identify what was agreed or where the agreed NFR baseline is recorded.
